It is more of a clinical book for professional hypnotists rather than a self-help one, so be careful about trying to introduce the case procedures described to yourself. Also be careful about taking the historical information at face value. Adam Eason, with Benjamin Parris, has an ISH article on self-hypnosis, dealing with self-directed learning and the question of another hypnotist and recordings.

It’s worth noting at this point that Nedergaard and Lupyan’s study, Not Everybody Has an Inner Voice (2024), was not investigating different adaptations of self hypnosis, but rather it was investigating people who reported having different amounts of inner speech. Thus, the questions in Quick start are not intended to be any sort of validated screening or test for ability to do self hypnosis, but merely a practical self-check.

paras: Memory, support, and choosing a practitioner

Chapter 7 of Peter Levine's "Trauma and Memory" (2015) is useful on the difference between a compelling experience and historical verification. The US Veterans Administration website has a good overview of hypnosis that includes some cautions about strong reactions and the potential of false memory creation. Here is a website from the American Society of Clinical Hypnosis (ASCH) that explains what hypnosis certification means. It separates professional preparation from a guarantee that someone is competent. The links already in the evidence and specialist sections point to their particular claims; they don’t validate every use of hypnosis.
